messages.subject: Problem with LOO(x, reloo = TRUE)
parts:
I'm fitting a model (let's call it q) in which I have to set the inits argument to 0 to avoid problems with initialization like this:

Rejecting initial value:
  Log probability evaluates to log(0), i.e. negative infinity.
  Stan can't start sampling from this initial value.

After running LOO on the model it turned out that one parameter has a Pareto k value larger than 0.7. I have thus tried:

LOO(q, reloo = TRUE)

After this call I get the same error as above. Could it be that LOO doesn't take the inits argument into account?

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Problem with LOO(x, reloo = TRUE)
parts:
If reloo = TRUE, the model is fit multiple times each leaving out one of the problematic observations.

To set inits = 0 during refitting go for

LOO(q, reloo = TRUE, update_args = list(inits = 0))
